title: Migrate to Mintlify with your agent
summary: We turned what we learned from hundreds of migrations into mint migrate, so your agent can move your docs from 21 platforms, prove nothing went missing, and tell you what didn't carry over.
body_markdown:
We've migrated hundreds of docs sites to Mintlify. We did the first ones by hand. Now agents do most of the work, but we noticed that they kept making the same mistakes.


They pasted shared content into every page instead of keeping it in one snippet. They copied resized images instead of the originals, so screenshots came out blurry. Pages moved and their old URLs stopped working.


Each time we fixed one of these, we wrote the fix into guides our internal agents use.[mint migrate](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/cli/commands#mint-migrate) ships those guides, so your agent can use them to move your docs too.


## Your agent starts with a guide for your platform


` mint migrate` has guides for 21 platforms, including ReadMe, GitBook, Docusaurus, Confluence, Jekyll and PDFs. Each one tells the agent what carries over and what doesn't. When something isn't in your export, like GitBook's OpenAPI specs, the agent knows to ask you for it.


Add your platform with` --from` , for example` mint migrate --agent claude --from gitbook` .


Moving from Flag Doesn't carry over


ReadMe` --from readme` Try It API key state, Recipes, custom HTML pages


GitBook` --from gitbook` Organization-level OpenAPI specs, visitor auth, integrations


Docusaurus` --from docusaurus` Swizzled components, custom React pages, Algolia config


Fern` --from fern`` generators.yml` SDK snippets, audiences, Ask Fern


Document360` --from document360` API specs, home page builder layouts, reader groups


Confluence` --from confluence` Page restrictions, dynamic macros, comments


Run` mint migrate` on its own to see every supported platform. If yours isn't on the list, the agent still follows the general workflow, and the[manual migration guide](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/migration/manual) covers the rest.


## It works from your repo, an export or your live site


You don't need your docs in a repo. The agent uses the best source you have, in this order:


1. **Your repo.** If your docs live in Git, the agent works from the source. Your navigation, URLs and OpenAPI spec come over exactly as your config declares them.
2. **An export.** For platforms behind a login, like Confluence, you export from the platform and the agent works from that folder.
3. **Your live site.** For hosted platforms with no repo, the agent saves a copy of every published page first, then converts from those files.


## The agent isn't done until it can prove it


The guides carry the rules we wrote after watching agents get migrations wrong. When the source keeps its shared files, each one becomes one snippet, imported wherever the source used it. Images come over at their original size. Every moved URL gets a redirect.


Before it hands the site back, the agent checks its own work:


- [mint validate](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/cli/commands#mint-validate) passes, so every page parses and builds.
- [mint broken-links](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/cli/commands#mint-broken-links) finds no broken links.
- A manifest lists every page from your source as done, excluded or blocked, with a reason for each one that isn't done. No page goes missing without a record.


Then the agent reports anything it couldn't carry over, such as a custom landing page or an embed with no Mintlify equivalent, so you decide what happens to it.


## Your docs stay with you


The migration runs on your machine, in your agent, under your own login. Your content never passes through Mintlify, and we never need your API keys.


The guides aren't a black box either. Every rule your agent follows is readable: run` mint migrate --topic conversion` to see how pages are converted, or` mint migrate --from gitbook` to see exactly how a GitBook site is handled.


## Get started


1. Install the Mintlify CLI:


```text
npm   i   -g   mint


```


Already have it? Update first, or run` npx mint@latest migrate` in place of` mint migrate` below.
2. Open a new folder for your Mintlify project and start a migration with your agent:


```text
mint   migrate   --agent   claude


```


Swap` claude` for` codex` ,` cursor` or` gemini` to use a different agent. The agent's own CLI needs to be installed first.
3. If you know your current platform, add it with` --from` :


```text
mint   migrate   --agent   claude   --from   gitbook


```


4. Tell your agent where your docs live: a repo path, an export folder or a URL.


Already working in an agent? Ask it to run` mint migrate` and follow the instructions. It pulls the guide for your platform and the detail for each step as it goes.


## From migrated to live


Once the migration checks out, your agent can publish it too.[mint deploy](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/cli/commands#mint-deploy) puts the site live, and` mint claim` attaches it to your Mintlify account. Your docs go from another platform to live on Mintlify without leaving the terminal.


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Which agents does it work with?**


` --agent` launches Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Gemini CLI. Any other agent can run` mint migrate` and follow the instructions it prints.


**What does it cost?**


` mint migrate` is free. The migration runs on your own agent subscription.


**What if my platform isn't listed?**


The agent follows the general workflow, which works for any docs framework. The[manual migration guide](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/migration/manual) covers the details.


**What happens to my API reference?**


The agent uses your existing OpenAPI spec. If you don't have one, it builds one from your reference pages only if you agree, and marks it as rebuilt in the report.


**What about versions and languages?**


The agent asks whether you want to bring them over, then maps them to Mintlify's versions and languages.


**Will my old URLs keep working?**


Yes. Every URL that moves gets a redirect, and the agent checks that each source URL resolves before it finishes.


**Can someone do the migration for me?**


Yes.[Talk to our team](https://www.mintlify.com/contact/sales) about a hands-on migration.
